steps.body: Now you know shapes from 3 sides all the way to 8: triangle, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon. Given any side count, you can name the shape.
Build a pentagon from its defining side count.

widget.prompt: Build a pentagon. Use the side control first; other attributes can vary without changing the family name.
widget.successFeedback: Five straight sides make a pentagon; size, tilt, and equal-side patterns are optional.
widget.sidesFeedback: A pentagon belongs to the five-sided family.
widget.attributesFeedback: For this family, side count is the defining rule. Return optional attributes to zero.

cml.actionGoal: Construct a polygon from the defining attribute of side count.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Change one non-defining attribute while preserving family membership. Which changes are legal?

explanation.prompt: Why can two shapes look different but belong to the same family?

options.label: They satisfy the same defining rules.
options.feedback: Yes — orientation and size are irrelevant to membership.

options.label: They must match one prototype picture.
options.feedback: A family includes every shape satisfying its rules.

predict.reveal: Shape names come from invariant attributes such as side count, right angles, equality, and parallelism.

explanationVariants: The smallest closed shape with straight sides is the triangle.

widget.prompt: A shape has 3 sides. What is it called? Tap it.

hotspots.label: pentagon
hotspots.feedback: A pentagon has 5 sides, not 3. The 3-sided shape is a triangle.

hotspots.label: hexagon
hotspots.feedback: A hexagon has 6 sides, not 3. The 3-sided shape is a triangle.

widget.missFeedback: Count the sides of each shape — the one with exactly 3 sides is the answer.

misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines ssg2 name any.

steps.body: Watch for near neighbors — heptagon (7) and octagon (8) are easy to mix up since they're next to each other in the count.

widget.prompt: A shape has 8 sides. What is it called?

options.label: octagon
options.feedback: Yes — 8 sides is an octagon.

options.label: heptagon
options.feedback: A heptagon has 7 sides, not 8. The 8-sided shape is an octagon.

options.label: hexagon
options.feedback: A hexagon has 6 sides, not 8. The 8-sided shape is an octagon.

steps.body: The full family, smallest to biggest: triangle (3), square/rectangle (4), pentagon (5), hexagon (6), heptagon (7), octagon (8).
Move one step past a pentagon.

widget.prompt: A polygon has one more side than a pentagon. What is it called?

options.label: hexagon
options.feedback: Yes — 6 sides is a hexagon.

options.label: heptagon
options.feedback: A heptagon has 7 sides, not 6. The 6-sided shape is a hexagon.

options.label: pentagon
options.feedback: A pentagon has 5 sides, not 6. The 6-sided shape is a hexagon.

explanationVariants: A polygon between a 6-sided hexagon and an 8-sided octagon has 7 sides: a heptagon.
More than 6 but fewer than 8 means 7, so the name is heptagon.

widget.prompt: Which polygon has more sides than a hexagon but fewer sides than an octagon?

options.label: heptagon
options.feedback: Yes — 7 sides is a heptagon.

options.label: octagon
options.feedback: An octagon has 8 sides, not 7. The 7-sided shape is a heptagon.

options.label: hexagon
options.feedback: A hexagon has 6 sides, not 7. The 7-sided shape is a heptagon.

explanationVariants: A pyramid comes to a point; a rectangular prism has a flat top.
Only the pyramid's triangle faces meet at one point.

widget.prompt: Which solid has faces that meet at a single point on top? Tap it.

hotspots.label: rectangular prism
hotspots.feedback: A rectangular prism has a flat top, not a point.

hotspots.label: cube
hotspots.feedback: A cube has a flat top, not a point.

widget.missFeedback: Look at each solid's top — tap the one whose faces climb to a single point.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — a pyramid comes to a point.

Fix the name by matching the exact side count: 7 means heptagon.

widget.prompt: Lee calls a 7-sided polygon an octagon. Which name fixes the mistake?

options.label: heptagon
options.feedback: Yes — 7 sides name a heptagon, so this corrects Lee's mix-up.

options.label: octagon
options.feedback: That repeats the mix-up. An octagon has 8 sides; 7 sides name a heptagon.

options.label: pentagon
options.feedback: A pentagon has 5 sides. The 7-sided polygon is a heptagon.

hints: Octagon means 8 sides, so that name cannot stay.

steps.body: You can name any shape from 3 to 8 sides, and tell the near-neighbor pairs apart.
takeaways: Triangle (3) through octagon (8) — the full family.
Heptagon and octagon are easy to mix up — check the exact count.
A square pyramid comes to a point; prisms have flat tops.

concept.body: Name a shape from its side count: triangle (3), square/rectangle (4), pentagon (5), hexagon (6), heptagon (7), octagon (8). Check the exact number carefully, especially for close neighbors like 7 and 8.

widget.prompt: A shape has 5 sides. What is it called?

options.label: pentagon
options.feedback: Yes — 5 sides is a pentagon.

options.label: hexagon
options.feedback: Hexagon is 6 sides; pentagon is 5.

options.label: heptagon
options.feedback: Heptagon is 7 sides; pentagon is 5.

concept.body: A square pyramid comes to a single point where its 4 triangle faces meet. A rectangular prism or cube, by contrast, has a flat top — no solid with a flat top is a pyramid.

explanationVariants: A pyramid comes to a point; a cube has a flat top.
Only the pyramid's faces meet at one point.

widget.prompt: Which solid has faces that meet at a single point on top?

options.label: square pyramid
options.feedback: Yes — a pyramid comes to a point.

options.label: cube
options.feedback: A cube has a flat top, not a point.

options.label: rectangular prism
options.feedback: A rectangular prism has a flat top, not a point.
